newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to probe parliament speaker over scandal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to probe parliament speaker over scandal.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors will question parliamentary speaker Kim Soo-han soon over allegations he took money from the founder of the Hanbo Group, who is now on trial for corruption, a government official said on Wednesday.
Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo had told prosecutors he had donated funds to Kim's parliamentary election campaign in 1992, the official said.

"Prosecutors decided to question the speaker under the principle that everyone, regardless of their position, will be investigated once they are involved in Hanbo-linked suspicions," the official told Reuters.
He said Kim was among 33 politicians named by Chung or his aides for having taken money from Hanbo as "political funds". Chung has denied bribing them.
The politicians include 20 lawmakers, including two tipped as possible candidates of the ruling New Korea Party in presidential elections due in December.

Chung is on trial on bribery and other charges along with nine others, including three close associates of President Kim Young-sam, in connection with the January collapse of Hanbo Steel Co, flagship of the country's 14th largest conglomerate.
